blocking.section: Ruralz Console / RBAC and SSO; Open questions (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-9)
blocking.issue: Residual. Separation of duties for Git commits depends on the commit's author and committer email, and anyone can set that email. OQ-9 keeps option (a), no commit-signature verification, and OQ-7 keeps option (a), no forge adapters, so Ruralz Control cannot tell who actually wrote or merged a commit. The attack: an `approver` who can merge authors a malicious commit under a colleague's email and merges it, which works where forge admins bypass branch protection. The approver's own verified email does not match, so RZ-CP-007 never fires and they approve their own prod change. The reverse attack also works. Commits spoofing every approver's email make RZ-CP-007 block all approvals, which stalls prod promotions, security fixes included. Security and identity has already answered OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-9 with option (b), and this document still shows (a) as current.
blocking.evidence: Line 477: "Approvers cannot approve a change they authored, committed (by verified email), wrote back, pushed, started or requested (`RZ-CP-007`, audited)". Line 603: "OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-9 | Verify Git commit signatures? | (a) No (current); (b) optionally". 08-security-and-identity.md line 472: "For OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-9, option (b): verify commit signatures where approvals depend on authorship".
blocking.fix: Adopt OQ-9 option (b) where `requireApproval` is set. Commit-based separation of duties uses only identities from verified commit signatures (author key bound to a Console user) or from forge adapter merge metadata. An unsigned or unverifiable commit is treated as authored by every approver-eligible user except those who explicitly attest otherwise, or requires two approvers. Say that a spoofed email can never block an approval by itself. Update the OQ-9 row to 'answered (b) by Security and identity' and add the spoofing case to the 'Compromised Git account' threat row.

blocking.section: Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle / Revision signing and verification (Rotation, emergency removal); Control Store and high availability / Fencing stale replicas; Audit and security
blocking.issue: Residual regression introduced by the new fence. An online key can sign any `assignmentSeq` and `promotionSeq`. The FSM enforces 'current plus one' only on the legitimate leader, and Nodes accept any higher pair within the current `storeEpoch`. An attacker who holds the stolen online key and has a delivery path signs an assignment and a promotion with a near-maximum sequence. Delivery paths the document admits: a stolen key-encryption key, which also yields the server CA key for 8091 impersonation; a compromised relay forwarding attacker-signed messages; or a compromised replica. Nodes activate the malicious Revision, promote it to Last-Known-Good and persist the huge sequence. Emergency removal then 'publishes a higher `version` and re-signs at once' at 'the next sequences'. Nothing says it opens a new `storeEpoch`, so every legitimate re-signed assignment is lower than the persisted pair and gets a transient NACK. Affected Nodes stay on the attacker's Revision and are quarantined. Under OQ-24 option (a) they also keep booting it as Last-Known-Good. The 'Stolen online key' and 'Stolen key-encryption key' threat rows claim recovery that the fence prevents. Promotions compare 'promotionSeq only', so the same lock applies to Last-Known-Good promotion, and after a restore that opens a new epoch.
blocking.evidence: Line 248: "Emergency removal publishes a higher `version` and re-signs at once, awaiting no ACK". Line 497: "Nodes persist the highest pair activated ... compare pairs in order and send a transient NACK for a lower one ... Promotions compare `promotionSeq` only with the last accepted promotion". Line 246: "a Last-Known-Good verified before an emergency removal still boots (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-24)". Line 580: "Stolen online key | ... a higher `version` removes the key". Line 581: "Stolen key-encryption key | Exposes online and CA keys: rotate the online key, Node CA and server CA".
blocking.fix: State that every emergency removal, and every server CA replacement, is a root-signed anchor set that opens a higher `storeEpoch`. Nodes compare both assignments and promotions as (`storeEpoch`, sequence) pairs, so a new epoch resets the attacker-inflated high-water marks. An emergency-removal anchor set carries a 'compromised since' time. After accepting it, a Node refuses to boot, as Last-Known-Good, any candidate or Last-Known-Good whose assignment or promotion was signed by the removed key after that time. Such a Node boots not ready or waits for the Control Stream, which amends OQ-24 for this case. Add the fence reset and this Last-Known-Good rule to the 'Stolen online key' and 'Stolen key-encryption key' threat rows.

blocking.section: GitOps model; Responsibilities and non-responsibilities; Audit and security
blocking.issue: Residual. The CRD source is now off by default, bound per namespace, audited and reported as Drift. The document still never says whether CRD-sourced Revisions pass `promotion.from` and `requireApproval`. For `ruralz bundle push` it states that promotion gating applies and that push is off by default under `requireApproval`. For CRDs it says nothing, and a CRD-sourced Revision has no commit, which is what promotion moves. The attack: once an operator binds a Kubernetes namespace to `prod`, any Kubernetes principal with write access to `ruralz.io` objects in that namespace can remove an `auth.*` Policy or widen a Plugin Capability. Those principals are often a broad namespace-admin group or a CI service account. The change then reaches prod with no `approver` and no separation of duties, only an after-the-fact Drift alert. That defeats the promise that `requireApproval` gates every prod Rollout.
blocking.evidence: Line 34: "Builds signed Revisions per Environment from Git, `ruralz bundle push` or opted-in CRDs". Line 186: "records the source tree digest in place of a commit, so promotion gating applies ... Push is per-Environment, off by default under `requireApproval`" (said for push only). Line 570: "The CRD source is off unless process configuration binds a namespace to an Environment." Line 439: "Git divergence | ... pushed Bundle or CRD source ... | Alert only, never reverted". Line 583: "CRDs bound, audited, reported as Drift".
blocking.fix: State that a CRD-sourced Revision records the digest of its source object set in place of a commit and passes `promotion.from` and `requireApproval` exactly like a pushed Bundle. Separation of duties treats the Kubernetes user as the author. By default, refuse a namespace binding to an Environment that sets `requireApproval`, mirroring push, and audit any override. Say whether `Environment` and `Cluster` CRDs are ever read. If they are, gate-relaxing changes made through them follow the same approval rule as `control/`. Extend the 'Malicious Bundle author or CRD writer' threat row accordingly.

non_blocking.section: Ruralz Console / RBAC and SSO; Certificates and replica join; Audit and security
non_blocking.suggestion: `admin` can mint a replica join token over REST (`/api/v1/replicas`, Settings 'join token') without step-up. A rogue voter can then commit raw Raft entries such as approvals, bindings and audit rewrites, bypassing separation of duties and audit. `admin` can also create a sock-puppet account and bind it `approver`. Limit join tokens to the host CLI, as restore already is. Require step-up plus an alert, or two-person control, for `approver` bindings. Add a 'Compromised admin account' threat row. Also say how a joining replica obtains the key-encryption key, and that `Join` never transfers it.

non_blocking.section: Control Store and high availability / Audit and security; Open questions
non_blocking.suggestion: Security and identity says chain heads MUST be exported off-box and that OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-12 should block Planned (M2). Without off-box heads, a compromised leader can rewrite the hash chain undetected. Mark OQ-12 as blocking for Planned (M2) and state that a restore appends a fork record.

Say that the `Enroll` lockout ('10 failures in 10 minutes') is per source, because a global lockout lets any unauthenticated caller deny Enrollment and break autoscaling (P4). State the token entropy (at least 128 bits). Check the token before `node.id` uniqueness so that RZ-CP-002 cannot probe enrolled IDs.

A hard per-account lockout after 10 failures lets anyone lock out every `approver` and stall prod promotions. Prefer per-account and per-source backoff. Throttle before PBKDF2 runs, since 600,000 iterations per attempt is a CPU denial-of-service vector against replicas that also hold Control Streams. Say whether API tokens can carry `admin`, `security-admin` or `approver` scopes, given that approvals require step-up TOTP.

non_blocking.section: Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle / Revision signing and verification
non_blocking.suggestion: Anchor sets are root-signed only, yet 'Rotate key (Settings or `/api/v1/trust`, `admin`)' is said to publish one. Say that Rotate key produces an unsigned draft that must be root-signed offline and uploaded, and name who uploads it. Say which Plugin trust policy wins, the one in process configuration or the one in an uploaded anchor set, and emit `trust-policy.changed`. Rotation step (2) waits for every connected Node, so one compromised Node that never ACKs stalls it. Quarantine and exclude such Nodes after N ACK timeouts (target).

Quarantined or lagging Nodes are not said to be excluded from later plans. An enrolled rogue Node that ACKs the current Revision can therefore veto every future Rollout in a small Cluster. Exclude quarantined Nodes from plans until they ACK the promoted digest. With fewer than 10 Nodes and `canary.percent: 10`, one canary Node's counters decide the gate, so treat single-Node gates as advisory.
